Heartland 4 Gombe 0, 31 March | biggest away win = Shooting Stars 0 Heartland 2, 15 May | highest scoring = Lobi Stars 3 Bayelsa United 4, 7 July | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest winless = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2012 Nigeria Premier League|2012]] | nextseason = [[2014 Nigeria Professional Football League|2014]] }} The '''2013 Nigeria Professional Football League''' was the 42nd season of the competition since its inception, and the 23rd since the rebranding of the league as the "Professional League". Due to start in December, numerous delays and challenges to the board pushed the opening weekend back to February, and then pushed to March 9. There was a season-opening Super Four tournament, won by [[Heartland F.C.]], between the four clubs involved in Continental competitions in order to get them ready for their international assignments.[http://www.goal.com/en-ng/news/4093/nigeria/2013/01/02/3643011/kano-state-we-are-grateful-to-the-nigeria-premier-league-for Kano promises to host a good Super Four tournament(Goal.com)] ==Clubs== Sixteen teams from the [[2012 Nigeria Premier League|previous season]] and four teams promoted from the [[Nigeria National League]] ([[Bayelsa United]], [[El-Kanemi Warriors]], [[Nasarawa United]] and [[Nembe City F.C.]]) participated in this season. {{location map+ |Nigeria |float=none |width=480 |caption=Locations of the '''Nigeria Premier League 2012–13''' teams |places= {{location map~ |Nigeria |lat=11.99 |long=8.52 |label= [[Kano Pillars F.C.|Kano Pillars]] |position=right}} {{location map~ |Nigeria |lat=4.77 |long=7.02 |label= [[Dolphins F.C. Pillars will play the rest of the season in Kaduna.
